$comment: The exact business and legal decisions this lane CANNOT make, and which keep specific
capabilities disabled until an operator supplies them.
Nothing here is a placeholder value waiting to be filled in by code. Every entry is a
decision with a named owner. Until each is supplied through its configuration port, the
corresponding capability stays fail-closed — the software does not guess a duration, a
jurisdiction, or an approval, and does not degrade to a permissive default.
No deletion is executed by anything in this repository. There is no deletion path at all;
the retention port decides eligibility and nothing consumes that decision to delete.
v2.0.0 makes every decision BLOCKING and machine-checkable. Each carries an explicit
unresolved placeholder for its owner and its resolution. NO REAL PERSON IS NAMED HERE and
no decision is pre-answered — assigning an owner is itself an operator act. The validator
in scripts/commissioning-decision-validator.mjs refuses commissioning while any required
decision is unresolved, so the package cannot be commissioned by forgetting.
v3.0.0 adds, for every decision, the four things an operator actually needs to act:
the required owner ROLE, the EVIDENCE that would resolve it, what it DEPENDS on, and the
exact FAIL-CLOSED behaviour until then. Owners remain __UNRESOLVED__ — naming a real
person would record an approval nobody gave, and choosing the person IS the decision.
raisedBy: Admin Enterprise acquisition / Shared Authority Hardening lane

decisions.question: How long may an enterprise outreach draft, and its approval receipts, be retained after creation or after a terminal state?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: A retention period is a legal and commercial commitment. Inventing one would create a policy nobody approved and would silently start deleting evidence.
decisions.port: RETENTION_PORT in src/components/admin/v2/outreachRepository.mjs and retentionDecision() in functions/src/outreachAuthority.ts
evidenceRequired: a written retention period with a policy version
the approver and the date
the legal basis
dependsOn: D3 legal hold authority — a hold must outrank retention, so hold authority is settled first
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: retentionDecision() returns retention_policy_unavailable for any policy that is absent, unapproved or version-less. No eligibility is calculated and nothing expires.

decisions.owner: Founder + legal counsel + data protection owner
decisions.question: Who may delete outreach records, under what recorded authority, and is deletion hard or is it tombstoning?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Receipts are append-only audit evidence. Deleting them is a deliberate legal act, not a maintenance task.
decisions.currentBehaviour: fail-closed; NO deletion path exists in the codebase
evidenceRequired: the deletion authority role
hard deletion or tombstoning
a policy version and approver
dependsOn: D1 retention duration — there is nothing to delete until a period exists
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: There is NO deletion path in the codebase. The port refuses, and scripts/commissioning-boundary-verify.mjs asserts that no deletion primitive exists in the server binding.

decisions.question: Who may place and lift a legal hold, and what evidence must a hold record carry?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: A hold is a legal instrument. The code can only enforce one it is told about.
decisions.currentBehaviour: three-valued: held / not held / UNKNOWN. Unknown BLOCKS. A failed read never degrades to 'not held'.
blocks: approving or transitioning a draft whose hold state cannot be determined
evidenceRequired: who may place and lift a hold
the fields a hold record must carry
a policy version
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: legalHoldState is three-valued. UNKNOWN blocks every transition; a FAILED read is unknown and never degrades to "not held".

decisions.question: For each jurisdiction, is outreach to an unsigned course legally approved, under which wording, opt-out mechanism and policy version?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: This lane is explicitly barred from authoring legal wording, opt-out language or jurisdiction policy. A default-allow would manufacture an approval nobody granted.
decisions.currentBehaviour: NO jurisdiction is approved. Every jurisdiction refuses. A truthy-but-not-true value such as 'pending' does not read as approval.
doesNotBlock: drafting, review and approval, which record an approval without transmitting anything
evidenceRequired: per-jurisdiction legal approval with wording and opt-out mechanism
a version string
approver and date
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: No jurisdiction is approved. jurisdictionDecision() requires legallyApproved === true AND a non-blank version; a truthy value such as "pending" does not read as approval. Every jurisdiction is unsendable.

decisions.question: Is outbound transmission to courses authorized at all, and through which provider under which contract?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Standing instruction for this lane is that nothing is transmitted. Enabling transmission is a founder decision.
decisions.currentBehaviour: false. There is no transmitter, no mail client and no outbound HTTP in the server binding. Even a fully approved draft in an approved jurisdiction reports not sendable, with the reason transmission_not_permitted.
evidenceRequired: founder authorization to transmit at all
the provider and contract reference
approver and date
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: TRANSMISSION_ENABLED is false and no transmitter exists — no mail client, no outbound HTTP. Even a fully approved draft in an approved jurisdiction reports not sendable with reason transmission_not_permitted.

decisions.question: Which App Check attestation provider is configured, for which project, and when does enforcement begin?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Provisioning is a Firebase console action plus a client attestation provider. Neither exists in this repository, and claiming enforcement without them would be a fabricated production state.
decisions.currentBehaviour: not_provisioned. REQUIRED_IN_PRODUCTION is true, so the port REFUSES rather than silently allowing; commissioningReadiness() reports not ready with the operator action named.
blocks: a truthful claim that privileged callables are attested
doesNotBlock: current operation, because enforcement is not yet switched on
decisions.knownInconsistency: The Partner Portal declares enforceAppCheck on ~56 privileged callables while the Admin lane declares it nowhere, and no client attestation provider exists in either. Either those callables would reject in production, or App Check is provisioned and the Admin callables are unprotected. This must be resolved before either lane deploys.
evidenceRequired: the attestation provider and its configuration
the project id it mints for
a monitoring period before enforcement
the enforcement date
dependsOn: D8 CI workflow — enforcement should not be switched on without a gate watching it
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: COMMISSIONING_STAGE is not_provisioned and REQUIRED_IN_PRODUCTION is true, so decideAppCheck REFUSES rather than silently allowing. No evidence can make the current stage allow. EXPECTED_PROJECT_ID is asserted against .firebaserc so enabling enforcement cannot silently refuse every real token.

decisions.question: Which existing admin_users records lack a canonical Active status, and should each be set Active or Suspended?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: It requires reading production data, which this lane is barred from, and a judgement about who is genuinely still staff.
requiredValues: a completed repair pass against the generated manifest
decisions.port: scripts/admin-status-migration-dryrun.mjs (read-only; generates a plan, applies nothing)
decisions.currentBehaviour: The allowlist denies any record without a canonical Active status, including the status-less shape the previous denylist admitted. Both in-product recovery paths require an ACTIVE Director.
blocks: safe activation of the allowlist in an environment with legacy records
doesNotBlock: the change itself, which is correct; this is a data-readiness step
decisions.severity: Highest risk in the manifest. The role allowlist added in this remediation widens the exposure: a record with a non-canonical ROLE now also loses access, and the dry-run reports those separately (non_canonical_spelling, unknown_role, obsolete_role) because the repair differs.
evidenceRequired: a completed dry-run against a real export with zero activation blockers
confirmation that at least one Director retains access
a record of every repaired document
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: The allowlist denies any record without a canonical Active status AND a canonical role. Both in-product recovery paths require an ACTIVE Director. scripts/admin-status-migration-dryrun.mjs refuses activation while any privileged record is non-conforming or no Director survives, and writes a repair plan it cannot execute.

decisions.topic: CI workflow ownership for the authority gates
decisions.question: Which workflow runs gate:admin-v2 / gate:admin-release, and on which branches, so the authority controls are enforced rather than remembered?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Adding a workflow to another lane's CI is a change to how that lane is gated, and choosing the trigger branches is an ownership decision.
decisions.currentBehaviour: No workflow invokes npm run gate, gate:admin-v2 or gate:admin-release. Every verifier in this package runs only when a human runs it.
blocks: any claim that the authority controls are continuously enforced
evidenceRequired: the workflow file that runs the aggregate gates
the branches it triggers on
confirmation that a failing gate blocks the merge
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: A workflow is now provided at .github/workflows/admin-authority-release.yml, but ADOPTING it — deciding the trigger branches and making it required — is an ownership act this lane cannot perform. The validator cross-checks the actual workflow state, so this decision cannot be marked resolved while no workflow runs the gates.

decisions.question: Who authors and deploys the single integrated ruleset covering every protected Admin and Portal collection?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Firestore replaces a ruleset wholesale, so authoring a partial one and deploying it would delete the rules for every collection it omits. This lane owns no canonical rules file and must not create one.
decisions.currentBehaviour: firebase.json binds NO ruleset, so no deploy from this tree can replace the project ruleset. The 21-line enterprise ruleset is rejected as a candidate for omitting 19 protected collections.
evidenceRequired: an integrated ruleset covering all 19 protected collections
its sha256, pinned in docs/INTEGRATED_RULES_ARTIFACT.json
a rules-suite run covering the 15-case test contract
dependsOn: D7 legacy status repair — rules that deny a locked-out admin compound the outage
decisions.failClosedBehaviour: No ruleset is bound in firebase.json, so a deploy cannot replace the project ruleset. renderDeployCommand() refuses to emit a deploy command while no complete, safe, hash-pinned artifact is bound.

invariants: No duration, jurisdiction, approval or policy value is invented anywhere in this repository.
Every port above fails CLOSED while its decision is outstanding; none degrades to a permissive default.
No deletion is executed. There is no deletion path.
Unknown legal-hold state blocks. It never collapses to 'not held'.
No decision in this manifest is pre-answered, and no real person is named. An unresolved owner is recorded as __UNRESOLVED__.
Commissioning is refused while any blocking decision is unresolved; there is no override.

commissioning.rule: Commissioning is refused while ANY blocking decision is unresolved. There is no partial commissioning and no override. Resolving a decision requires evidence recorded outside this document wherever external corroboration is possible.
requiredOrder: D7 legacy status repair — FIRST. Activating the status AND role allowlists without it can lock out every Director, and there is no in-product recovery.
D8 CI workflow adoption — SECOND, so every later step is continuously verified rather than checked once by hand.
D6 App Check provisioning — THIRD. The Portal already declares enforceAppCheck on ~56 callables with no provider; this is the largest live gap.
D9 Firestore integrated ruleset — FOURTH, and before any deploy.
D3 legal hold authority — FIFTH. Holds outrank retention, so this settles before retention.
D1 and D2 retention and deletion — SIXTH.
D5 transmission authorization — LAST, and only after every item above.
